output.summary: A perennial herbaceous mint hybrid indigenous to Europe and the Middle East. It usually produces no seed and spreads rapidly through runners, bearing dark-green leaves and purple flowers. Fresh or dried leaves are commonly brewed as tea and used to flavour foods, sweets and drinks.
output.edibilityNote: Fresh or dried leaves are used in tea and to flavour foods, sweets, preserves, alcoholic drinks and chewing gum.
